title.purpose: Pane headings and modal/section titles only (20px, 19px, 15px variants share this role).

body.purpose: The base UI size — nearly all text in the app.

small.purpose: Secondary text — hints, sub-labels, result rows, muted supporting lines under a heading.

micro.purpose: Compact badges and tags (.tag, event badges) where Label's uppercase 12px treatment would be too loud.

label.purpose: Uppercase structural labels: table headers, form group labels, section headers.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: The one shadow documented in DESIGN.md (dark theme), for layers that float above normal page flow: popover menus, dialogs, toasts, the settings save bar.

shadows.name: float-hover-lift
shadows.purpose: `--shadow-float`: a second, undocumented shadow token used only for the live-grid tile hover-lift (`.tile:hover`, 2px translateY). Not in DESIGN.md's Shadow Vocabulary, which names only one shadow in the system — recorded here as build fact, not folded into the documented rule.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Hover/press micro-feedback: borders, backgrounds, opacity (tile-actions show/hide, toggle track).

motion.name: dur-base
motion.purpose: Zoom/pan transforms and the tile's own hover transform/box-shadow transition.

motion.name: dur-slow
motion.purpose: Larger UI motion: auto-hiding playback controls, fullscreen side-panel slide-ins.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Applied today on `.tile`'s hover transform/shadow and `.tile-actions`'s show/hide — the formalized default easing for ordinary UI motion (per app.css's own redesign-v2 comment).

motion.name: ease-spring
motion.purpose: Defined per app.css's comment for gesture-release and toggle-confirmation moments, but not yet wired to any rule in app.css as of this phase-1 tokens pass — a reserved, not-yet-consumed token.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one emphasized action in a group — save, confirm, primary CTA.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 7px; height: 36px; padding: 0 13px; border-radius: var(--r-sm, 8px); border: 1px solid transparent; font: 600 14px/1 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: filter var(--dur-fast, .15s) ease, background var(--dur-fast, .15s) ease, border-color var(--dur-fast, .15s) ease; } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--accent, #0074e8); border-color: var(--accent, #0074e8); color: var(--accent-ink, #ffffff); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.08); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #0074e8); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Default button style for non-primary actions (the plain `.btn`).
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 7px; height: 36px; padding: 0 13px; border-radius: var(--r-sm, 8px); font: 500 14px/1 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color var(--dur-fast, .15s) ease; } .ds-btn-secondary { background: var(--panel-2, #1a2029); border: 1px solid var(--line-2, #313b4a); color: var(--text, #e7ebf1); } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { border-color: var(--faint, #5c6878); }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 7px; height: 36px; padding: 0 13px; border-radius: var(--r-sm, 8px); border: 1px solid transparent; font: 500 14px/1 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background var(--dur-fast, .15s) ease, color var(--dur-fast, .15s) ease; } .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: var(--muted, #8b97a8); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: var(--panel-2, #1a2029); color: var(--text, #e7ebf1); }

components.name: Toggled Button (aria-pressed)
components.description: A button in its pressed/active state (aria-pressed="true") — layout pickers, filter toggles.
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 7px; height: 36px; padding: 0 13px; border-radius: var(--r-sm, 8px); font: 500 14px/1 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-pressed { background: var(--accent-soft, rgba(0, 116, 232, .16)); border: 1px solid var(--accent, #0074e8); color: var(--accent, #0074e8); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Standard text/password/number field used across Settings.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; height: 36px; padding: 0 11px; border-radius: var(--r-sm, 8px); border: 1px solid var(--line-2, #313b4a); background: var(--bg, #0b0e13); color: var(--text, #e7ebf1); font: 400 14px/1 -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Inter, ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-input:hover { border-color: var(--faint, #5c6878); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #0074e8); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Toggle Switch
components.description: The only binary on/off control style in the system.
components.css: .ds-switch { position: relative; display: inline-block; width: 38px; height: 22px; } .ds-switch input { position: absolute; inset: 0; opacity: 0; margin: 0; cursor: pointer; z-index: 1; } .ds-switch span { position: absolute; inset: 0; border-radius: var(--r-full, 999px); background: var(--line-2, #313b4a); transition: background var(--dur-fast, .15s); } .ds-switch span::after { content: ''; position: absolute; top: 3px; left: 3px; width: 16px; height: 16px; border-radius: 50%; background: #fff; transition: transform var(--dur-fast, .15s); } .ds-switch input:checked + span { background: var(--accent, #0074e8); } .ds-switch input:checked + span::after { transform: translateX(16px); } .ds-switch input:focus-visible + span { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #0074e8); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Live-Count Pill
components.description: The actual `.pill` + `.dot` combination used in Live's topbar ('N/M live'); the dot is Live Red when every tile is live, Warn Amber ('wait') otherwise. Pills never pair with an Armed Green dot in the build.
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; height: 24px; padding: 0 9px; border-radius: var(--r-full, 999px); background: var(--panel-2, #1a2029); border: 1px solid var(--line, #262e3a); font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted, #8b97a8); white-space: nowrap; } .ds-dot { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--faint, #5c6878); flex: none; } .ds-dot-live { background: var(--live, #ff453a); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px var(--live-soft, rgba(255,69,58,.16)); }

components.name: Success Result / Badge
components.description: The real Armed Green usage: a passed connection test (`.result.ok`) or an 'On'/'2FA' status badge (`.badge.ok`) — success/healthy state, never a live indicator.
components.css: .ds-badge-ok { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 20px; padding: 0 7px; border-radius: var(--r-full, 999px); font-size: 11.5px; font-weight: 600; background: var(--armed-soft, rgba(52,211,153,.14)); border: 1px solid var(--armed, #34d399); color: var(--armed, #34d399); white-space: nowrap; }

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: Topbar/side-rail navigation item (icon + label); Accent Blue Soft background + Accent Blue text marks the current page (aria-current="page").
components.html: Live
components.css: .ds-nav-link { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; padding: 7px 12px; border-radius: var(--r-sm, 8px); color: var(--muted, #8b97a8); text-decoration: none; font-weight: 500; } .ds-nav-link:hover { background: var(--panel-2, #1a2029); color: var(--text, #e7ebf1); } .ds-nav-link-active { background: var(--accent-soft, rgba(0, 116, 232, .16)); color: var(--accent, #0074e8); } .ds-nav-icon { width: 18px; height: 18px; flex: none; }

components.name: Card
components.description: The primary content container across Settings and Events.
components.html:
Recorder connection

Address, login, and encryption.
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--panel, #131820); border: 1px solid var(--line, #262e3a); border-radius: var(--r-lg, 12px); padding: 18px 20px; } .ds-card h3 { margin: 0 0 3px; font-size: 14.5px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--text, #e7ebf1); } .ds-card-sub { margin: 0; color: var(--muted, #8b97a8); font-size: 13px; }

components.name: The Eye Mark
components.description: Signature mark (`.brand-mark`): a ring-and-dot iris in Accent Blue on a dark square. Used in the topbar brand lockup — the only purely-identity use of the accent color. The square's own background (`#111827`) is a literal, not a themed/custom-property token.
components.css: .ds-eyemark { display: inline-grid; place-items: center; width: 26px; height: 26px; border-radius: var(--r-sm, 8px); background: #111827; } .ds-eyemark::before { content: ''; width: 12px; height: 12px; border-radius: 50%; border: 2.5px solid var(--accent, #0074e8); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px #111827, inset 0 0 0 5px var(--accent, #0074e8); }

narrative.overview:
Redesign v2 (see `ROADMAP.md`) keeps the Watch Room's calm, low-contrast, stare-at-it-for-hours character but moves from one color carrying three meanings to four colors each carrying exactly one: a system blue for everything interactive (selected, primary, focus, in progress), red for "this is live right now," green for "this succeeded / is healthy," and amber/purple for the two event categories that need their own identity (motion, tamper). Nothing is decorative — every one of those four still only appears when it's specifically meaningful, never ambient — but status and selection no longer compete for the same pixel the way a single accent forced them to. Spacing stays tight, controls stay compact (28–36px), numbers stay tabular, and the interface still gets out of the way of the footage it exists to show.

The controls themselves lean refined rather than purely mechanical: hover and pressed states get real (if subtle) treatment — brightness shifts, soft accent washes, ring outlines, a couple of places real spring motion — so the density reads as considered, not thrown together.
keyCharacteristics: Dark by default (`color-scheme: dark`), with a fully-specified light theme as a first-class alternate, not an afterthought.
Four semantic colors, each with exactly one job: blue = interactive, red = live, green = success/healthy, amber/purple = event category. Never mixed, never decorative.
Flat surfaces at rest; shadow appears only on things that float above the normal layout.
Small, functional type scale — no hero/display type anywhere; this is an instrument panel, not a marketing page.
Tabular numerals on every timestamp, clock, duration, zoom percentage, and count.

rules.name: The On-Video Invariance Rule
rules.body: Anything painted directly over live footage (badges, overlays, ROI boxes, floating transport controls) stays fixed across light/dark theme — the video itself never re-themes, so its chrome shouldn't either. Everything else in this document does adapt per theme; this is the one deliberate exception.

rules.name: The One-Job-Per-Color Rule
rules.body: Accent Blue is the only color used for emphasis, selection, or primary action — if a control isn't active, selected, or the primary action in its group, it does not get colored, it stays gunmetal/muted. Live Red, Armed Green and Tamper Purple are each scoped the same way to their own single status meaning; none of the four ever stands in for another, and none is used decoratively.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every numeric read-out — the clock, timestamps, durations, zoom percentage, event counts — uses `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, so digits never shift width as they change on a screen meant to be glanced at repeatedly.

rules.name: The Floating-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: If it's part of the normal page layout, it's flat with a border. If it floats above the layout (menu, dialog, toast, save bar), it gets the Float shadow. Nothing in between.

rules.name: The Pill-for-Status Rule
rules.body: Full-round shape is reserved for things that represent state or a compact choice (status pills, event badges, quality tags, toggles). Containers that hold content — cards, tiles, dialogs — never go fully round; they stay in the 8–14px range.

dos: Do treat each of the four semantic colors as a state signal first — reach for Accent Blue when something is selected, primary, or on; Live Red only for live status; Armed Green only for success/healthy; never as general brand color to sprinkle around.
Do keep numeric displays (clocks, timestamps, durations, percentages, counts) on tabular numerals.
Do keep containers flat with a 1px border; reserve the Float shadow strictly for popovers, dialogs, toasts, and the save bar.
Do use full-round shape only for status/selection chips and toggles, never for content containers.
donts: Don't introduce a fifth semantic hue for "brand" purposes — warn-amber, danger-red and info-teal stay semantic-only, and the four redesign-v2 colors already cover interactive/live/success/event-category meaning between them.
Don't add shadow to any surface that's part of the normal page flow (cards, tiles, panels, topbar) — that's reserved for floating layers only.
Don't add a display/hero type size anywhere; this is an Operate-mode instrument panel, not a marketing surface, and the type scale stays functional.

Don't widen the touch/click targets or padding much past the current compact scale (28–36px control heights) — density is a deliberate trait of a screen meant for long monitoring sessions, not a gap to close.
